title: The Looping Pangram
subtitle: As the storyteller whispers, a soft shadow falls on the living and the dead.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: After this reset, we need to limit the changes inside the toybox as much as possible.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: That is to say, the fewer the people who enter the toybox, the better.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: It's best we only send one person.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: I'll do you one better: don't send anyone in and blow it to kingdom come!

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Researcher Medicine Pocket.
Medicine Pocket rolls their eyes and keeps talking, unfazed by the warning in Ulrich's tone.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Great, a brand new toybox, and a brand new chance to fail! Consistently reproducing failed results follows the scientific method, too, right?

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Seriously. None of us even knows what's in there, and you're saying we should send a single person in alone?

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: You're totally fine with that, huh? Leaving all those insane pieces and that psycho raven for some unlucky bastard to deal with?

items.speaker: X
items.text: This doesn't happen often, but I have to say I agree with Medicine Pocket. Whoever decides to enter will be risking their own safety.
Medicine Pocket rolls their eyes again. X and Ulrich have clearly missed the point.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Ugh. What I was saying is that we shouldn't be wasting our brainpower on this thing.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: We also need to consider the pieces. They may just be data to us, but to them, this is their entire world. We must avoid destroying it if we can.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Oh, my dear Ulrich, I'm moved to pieces! If only the real "Storm" shared your glowing sense of humanitarianism.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Pardon, can I interrupt for a second?
Hissabeth knocks on the table.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: I have good news. I've tested the communicator's durability.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Although the tower's effect grows stronger the closer you get, the unlucky person entering the box will be able to receive outside help up until they enter the tower. If we aren't giving up on that plan, that is.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: That's great, but assigning a hundred people to wash test tubes in a lab isn't gonna make the research go any faster.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: That's all that communicator's gonna give. A bunch of test tube washers.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Don't say that. If you gave me ten research assistants who understood the Lane-Emden equation, I'd be pleased no matter what.
For once, Enigma listens. He waits until Hissabeth is done before he speaks.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: What I meant is that I will go.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: You're a human, Adler. And at the end of the day, that toybox runs on arcanum.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Thank you for the reminder, Bottlebrain.
Enigma's tone is polite, but his expression is grim.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I'm certain you will all provide more help than test tube washing, like capturing arcane fluctuations and relaying the data through the communicator.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Besides, I'm the cryptographer here.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I doubt any one of you has undergone even a fraction of the cryptographic training required to reverse-engineer a key from an as-of-yet unknown cipher.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Well, I certainly haven't.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: But I believe I understand now. You think Ulrich has a point, too. Humanitarian care, no?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Where on earth did you get that impression?
He turns away, but his darkening expression doesn't escape Hissabeth's notice.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Alright, you're right. You didn't say that.
She shrugs and clears the way for Enigma.
A faint dizziness blurs Enigma's vision.
Lake, Toybox
Everything has changed.
Frowning, Enigma pats his wet coat, sending little streams down into the moonlit water below—assuming that is indeed moonlight and water.

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Woah, look at that ball of light in the sky! Hah, I'm starting to like this place!

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I'm afraid that's this toybox's version of the moon.
He pulls himself upright against the knee-high silver lines and wades unsteadily toward the shore.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Hey, those fir trees over there look like snowflakes.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Why don't you tell me something I don't know?

items.speaker: X
items.text: Alright. I just thought some talk on Koch curves might lighten the topic.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Can anyone tell me how to mute this thing?
Enigma distances himself from the communicator as another wave of commotion erupts on the other end. A moment later, Ulrich's calm voice comes through.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Understood. Researcher Pointer and I will strictly control the others' input as requested.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Umm, right, we guarantee we'll only bother you if it's essential.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Thank you. I'll contact you if necessary.
He switches off the communicator, yet the surrounding noise persists.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Who's there?
Not far off, a young piece turns around, hands twisted together nervously.

items.speaker: "Marcus"
items.text: Mr. Enigma?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Didn't expect I'd run into you here, "Ms. Marcus."

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Are you reading?
He points at the thin white cuboid in the piece's hand.

items.speaker: "Marcus"
items.text: Yes, Mr. Enigma, I-I'm reading a story. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: That's the story? Ah, I understand.

items.speaker: "Marcus"
items.text: Mhmm. It's about legends and people who write history. I haven't finished it yet. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
She smiles shyly. What used to be a book has slowly flattened into a colorless, almost depthless shape.

items.speaker: "Marcus"
items.text: Is there something I can help you with? Quick.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I'm looking for a tower. Do you know where it might be?

items.speaker: "Marcus"
items.text: It seems—fox—a lot of people are looking for that tower ... It—quick—might be on the other side of the forest.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Thank you.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Ms. Marcus. Would you like to come with me?
She looks bewildered. The book finally loses the last of its depth and slides from her arms.

items.speaker: "Marcus"
items.text: I'm waiting for someone. How—quick—strange. I-I don't seem to remember who I'm waiting for. Brown.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Was she also looking for the tower?

items.speaker: "Marcus"
items.text: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Forget it.
Enigma hesitates, then crouches to pick the book up for her. But it slips through his fingers, like the moon's reflection slipping from cupped hands.
He shakes his head and gives up. It's useless anyway.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I should go, Ms. Marcus. Goodbye.
He strides away. The girl's voice follows after him.

items.speaker: "Marcus"
items.text: Please—brown—be careful! There's a fox, brown in the forest. Lazy dog!

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Thank you.
Following the piece's direction, Enigma squints into the distance. The white tower's spire rises above a sea of treetops.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Hah. How wonderfully eye-catching. What is this, Tantalus's punishment?
Another figure emerges from the shadows of the trees.

items.speaker: Laplace Researcher I
items.text: Danger. Closer don't any come!

items.speaker: Laplace Researcher I
items.text: Wait, you're ...?!
He knows this researcher. The toybox is pulling from his buried memories.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: It's me. A tiny, insignificant cryptographer.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: It's a pity we've never worked together.
The communicator rings again. Whether it's at the worst moment or the best one, he can't decide.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Adler, how bad is it?
He subconsciously reaches into his pocket. The metal tube is cold against his fingers.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Oh, fine. Just a piece who's gone mad.
Enigma looks up at the top of the tower for what feels like the thousandth time. It's faintly glowing.
He raises the communicator.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: We have a problem.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Even after all this walking, I haven't gotten any closer to the Tower of Babel.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: If anything, it appears to be growing farther and farther away.
